rulers.title: Prince of Upper Hungary ('King of Upper Hungary' in the Thököly article)
rulers.note: Infobox 'Ruler: 1682-1685: Emeric Thököly'; the Thököly page: 'the title of King of Upper Hungary', reign as Prince of Upper Hungary 1682 to 1685, seized by the Turks at Nagyvárad in 1685.

correction.text: the same land as the 1683 shape: the principality 'established on 19 November 1682', capital Kassa, which 'encompassed most of present-day Slovakia', part of north-eastern Hungary and small parts of western Ukraine and northern Romania

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row starts in 1683, the infobox says 'Established: November 19, 1682'. The 1683 shape is used for 1682.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid for 1683-1685 only: the infobox gives 'Disestablished: October 15, 1685' and the page says 'his realm ceased to exist' after Thököly's defeat at Eperjes; Cliopatria's 1686 year belongs to the successors

keyframe_review.note: 65,917 km2 (bbox 17.91-23.42E, 46.87-49.38N, Slovakia, Hungary, Ukraine). The page gives no area. Its description (most of Slovakia, part of north-eastern Hungary, small parts of western Ukraine and northern Romania) fits the shape; the Thököly page adds that he 'extended his dominions to the Vág (Slovak: Váh) river'. 23,014 km2 of the shape (91 cells) is the Nikolsburg land that Cliopatria draws in Transylvania until 1682 and from 1687 (confidence 1 transfers in both ledgers). Cliopatria's Habsburg Monarchy shape lacks the Slovak part until 1687, so 1686 is a hole in Cliopatria; the Habsburg dossier's 1685 gain fills it. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1683..1685 from this entry's own 'valid for 1683-1685 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

region.text: Kassa and Upper Hungary: the principality 'encompassed most of present-day Slovakia', part of north-eastern Hungary and 'small parts of western Ukraine and northern Romania'

ledger.note: 1682: Thököly founds the Principality of Upper Hungary at Kassa as an Ottoman vassal. 'The principality was established on 19 November 1682'; it was a 'short-lived vassal state of the Ottoman Empire' that 'agreed to pay 20,000 gold coins to the Ottomans annually' (the Thököly page says 'an annual tribute of 40,000 Thalers' and the title 'King of Upper Hungary'). Imre Thököly had led the rising since 1680 with Ottoman and Transylvanian support. The page gives the extent in words; the drawn land is Cliopatria's 1683 shape without the part Transylvania held.

region.text: the north-western counties inside the principality's shape ('part of northeastern Hungary, and small parts of western Ukraine and northern Romania')

ledger.note: 19 November 1682: 23,014 km2 that Cliopatria holds in Transylvania up to 1682 lie in Upper Hungary from 1683. The page says the rising was 'supported and sustained by the Ottoman state and the Principality of Transylvania' but not that land passed; a bridging reading from Cliopatria's shapes (page silent).

region.text: Eperjes (Prešov) and its surroundings, where Thököly was defeated in 1685

ledger.note: 1685: the Habsburg campaign reaches Upper Hungary. 'However, the campaign of 1685 was a series of disasters' and 'he was defeated at Prešov (Eperjes)'. The page gives no month and no detail of the Habsburg advance; the radius around Prešov is the only place it names in the fighting (Cliopatria's Habsburg 1687 shape is the next evidence of Habsburg control).

15 October 1685: the contest ends with the realm. In 1685 Thököly 'was defeated at the Battle of Eperjes' and 'his realm ceased to exist' (infobox 'Disestablished: October 15, 1685'); the Thököly page: the Turks seized him at Nagyvárad and 'most of his followers made their peace with the Emperor'.

region.text: Upper Hungary: Slovakia and the north-eastern Hungarian part, which the infobox gives to the 'Kingdom of Hungary' under the Habsburg king

ledger.note: 15 October 1685: Upper Hungary reverts to the Habsburg king of Hungary. Infobox 'Succeeded by: Kingdom of Hungary'; the habsburg-monarchy dossier records the matching gain on the same date. The page does not describe the reconquest.

region.text: the north-western counties drawn in Transylvania again from 1687

ledger.note: 15 October 1685: the north-western counties go back to the Transylvania row of Cliopatria (1687 shape). The page is silent on who held them after the realm ended; bridging reading, matching the gain in the principality-of-transylvania dossier.

15 October 1685: Thököly's principality ceases to exist. 'In 1685 Thököly was defeated at the Battle of Eperjes (present-day Prešov). The Turks imprisoned him because of his earlier negotiations with Leopold, and his realm ceased to exist.'

wars.name: Thököly's uprising

zones.text: Eperjes (Prešov), where Thököly was defeated in 1685

wars.outcome: Thököly's war 'began in 1678'; Eastern Hungarian Kingdom lands and 'central Hungarian mining towns were soon in Thököly's possession'; the Ottomans recognized him in 1682 as Prince (King) of Upper Hungary; the 1685 campaign 'was a series of disasters', he was beaten at Prešov and seized by the Turks at Nagyvárad.
wars.note: Not a Wikipedia article title; the Thököly page carries the account. The Principality of Upper Hungary page dates his leadership of the rebellion to 1680.

wars.name: Battle of Vienna
wars.outcome: 'Thököly materially assisted the Turks in the Battle of Vienna in 1683'; the Ottoman defeat began the Habsburg reconquest of Hungary.
wars.note: No territorial result for this principality; listed so the reviewer can see it was considered.

certainty.note: A short-lived rebel-and-vassal state with no treaty or survey line; the western frontier ran to the Váh river approximately.

notes: Written by eu-15-k on 2026-10-25 from two pages. (1) Cliopatria's 1683-1686 shape runs one year past the page's end (15 October 1685) and starts one year after 19 November 1682; both corrected as keyframes. (2) The two pages disagree on tribute (20,000 gold coins against 40,000 Thalers a year) and on the title (Prince in the infobox, King in the Thököly article); neither changes the map. (3) The OTTOMAN SUZERAINTY (vassal tint, rule 4) is not in the ottoman-empire dossier: it has no vassal_start/vassal_end for principality-of-upper-hungary (19 November 1682 to 15 October 1685); the me-10 group should add them, with this dossier's region. (4) The 23,014 km2 shared with Transylvania is the weakest point: both dossiers carry it at confidence 1 from Cliopatria's shapes. A gap-filler should open the Wikipedia articles 'Royal Hungary' or 'Kuruc' for who held Szatmár, Bereg and Ugocsa in 1683-1685. (5) The pages do not give the Habsburg reconquest of 1685 (the Great Turkish War page, opened for the Transylvania dossier, has Eperies, Kaschau and Tokaj falling soon after 19 August 1685 and Caprara's victory near Kassa in 1685), so the date of the principality's collapse on the ground may be a few months before the infobox's 15 October. (6) The Thököly page also records his election as Prince of Transylvania (22 September-25 October 1690); not this dossier. No gazetteer names unknown.
